Infusion Day Note, 2033-04-06

This 78-year-old patient with relapsed mantle cell lymphoma received autologous CD19-directed CAR-T cells at 13:15 today, three days after completing fludarabine and cyclophosphamide lymphodepletion. The infusion was uneventful, with no fever, rash or change in blood pressure during or after the product was given.

Comorbidities include type 2 diabetes managed with metformin, osteoarthritis of both knees, and cataract surgery on both eyes some years ago with good vision since; the patient reads without difficulty and wears no hearing aids.

Before the infusion, at 11:30, the bedside ICE screen was 10/10, and the neurological examination was unremarkable, with symmetric strength and a steady gait.

Plan: ICE screening twice daily and with any change, vital signs every four hours, levetiracetam prophylaxis, and early mobilisation with physical therapy.
